circuit:Abu Dhabi.title: Yas Marina Circuit
circuit:Abu Dhabi.summary: Yas Marina Circuit, a 5. 281 km track designed by Hermann Tilke on Yas Island in Abu Dhabi, has been the venue for the season-closing Formula One race since 2009. It represents the second Middle Eastern Formula One circuit to be constructed, following Bahrain and preceding later additions in Qatar and Saudi Arabia.

circuit:Australia.title: Albert Park Circuit
circuit:Australia.summary: The Albert Park Circuit is a street track that encircles Albert Park Lake in Melbourne's Albert Park suburb and hosts the Formula One Australian Grand Prix each year alongside various support series races. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 certification status.

circuit:Austria.title: Red Bull Ring
circuit:Austria.summary: The 4. 326 km circuit located in Spielberg, Austria, originally operated as the Österreichring and served as the venue for the Austrian Grand Prix throughout the 1970s and 1980s. Following renovation and reconfiguration, the track was renamed and resumed hosting the Austrian Grand Prix from 1997 until the early 2000s.

circuit:Azerbaijan.title: Baku City Circuit
circuit:Azerbaijan.summary: The Baku City Circuit is a street track in Azerbaijan's capital city, situated near Baku Boulevard and spanning 6. 003 km, which ranks as the fourth-longest venue in the modern Formula One calendar. The circuit first hosted a Formula One race in 2016 as the European Grand Prix, before being officially designated as the Azerbaijan Grand Prix starting in 2017, with operations managed by the Baku City Circuit Operation Company.

circuit:Bahrain.title: Bahrain International Circuit
circuit:Bahrain.summary: Opened in 2004, the Bahrain International Circuit spans 5. 412 km and has hosted the annual Formula One Bahrain Grand Prix, marking the motorsport's inaugural Middle Eastern race. The FIA Grade 1-licensed venue accommodates various racing categories including GP2 Series and endurance competitions, while featuring multiple circuit configurations for different events.

circuit:Barcelona.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Barcelona.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km Spanish circuit is renowned for its balanced design featuring extended straights combined with diverse corner configurations, making it an excellent test of overall racing capability. The venue holds FIA Grade 1 status and can accommodate approximately 140,700 spectators across its grandstand facilities.

circuit:Belgium.title: Circuit de Spa-Francorchamps
circuit:Belgium.summary: This Belgian circuit spanning 7. 004 kilometres near the town of Spa has hosted Formula One racing since 1950, making it one of the sport's oldest venues. The track has maintained its Grand Prix status continuously from 1985 onward, with only two exceptions in 2003 and 2006, and currently serves as the home of the Belgian Grand Prix.

circuit:Canada.title: Circuit Gilles Villeneuve
circuit:Canada.summary: Located on Notre Dame Island in Montreal, Quebec, this 4. 361 km circuit serves as the home of the Formula One Canadian Grand Prix. Beyond Formula One, the track has hosted various international racing series including sports car championships, open-wheel competitions, and NASCAR events throughout its history.

circuit:China.title: Shanghai International Circuit
circuit:China.summary: Shanghai International Circuit, located in the Jiading district of Shanghai, is a motorsport facility most recognized as the home of the Chinese Grand Prix, which took place there from 2004 to 2019 before returning in 2024. The venue also began hosting the Shanghai ePrix electric racing championship starting in 2024.

circuit:Great Britain.title: Silverstone Circuit
circuit:Great Britain.summary: Silverstone, located in Northamptonshire, England, has been the primary venue for the British Grand Prix since 1948 and notably hosted the inaugural World Championship race in 1950. After sharing hosting duties with Aintree and Brands Hatch during the 1955-1986 period, the circuit became the permanent home of Britain's Formula One round from 1987 onwards, and continues to stage other major motorsport events including MotoGP.

circuit:Hungary.title: Hungaroring
circuit:Hungary.summary: The Hungaroring, a 4. 381 km track located near Budapest in Hungary, hosted the inaugural Formula One Grand Prix held within the Eastern Bloc in 1986. Built in just eight months following a government decision to construct it outside the city rather than as a street circuit in Budapest's main park, the venue held its inaugural race that March as a tribute to Hungary's pioneering motorcycle racing champion.

circuit:Italy.title: Autodromo Nazionale Monza
circuit:Italy.summary: Located near Milan in northern Italy, the Monza Circuit is a 5. 793 km track constructed in 1922 as mainland Europe's oldest purpose-built racing venue. It has continuously hosted the Italian Grand Prix since 1949, making it one of only four circuits to appear on every Formula One calendar since the sport's inception, and earned its nickname "Temple of Speed" because of its extended straights and fast-paced corner design.

circuit:Japan.title: Suzuka International Racing Course
circuit:Japan.summary: Suzuka Circuit, a 5. 807 km figure-eight track in Mie Prefecture, Japan, serves as a premier venue for Formula One and Super Formula racing. Operated by Honda Mobilityland and capable of accommodating 155,000 spectators, the facility has established itself as one of motorsport's most significant racing grounds.

circuit:Las Vegas.title: Las Vegas Strip Circuit
circuit:Las Vegas.summary: The Las Vegas Strip Circuit is a street-based racing course located in Paradise, Nevada that follows roads through the iconic Las Vegas Boulevard and its surrounding area. The track passes by some of the city's most recognizable destinations, including major casino resorts and the MSG Sphere entertainment venue. This urban circuit forms part of Formula One's racing calendar in the region.

circuit:Mexico City.title: Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez
circuit:Mexico City.summary: Located in Mexico City, the 4. 304 km Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez commemorates two Mexican racing brothers who both died in motorsport accidents during the 1960s and early 1970s. The venue has hosted Formula One's Mexican Grand Prix since 2015 on its current layout, resuming a tradition that previously ran during two separate eras ending in 1992.

circuit:Miami.title: Miami International Autodrome
circuit:Miami.summary: The Miami International Autodrome is a temporary circuit constructed around Hard Rock Stadium in Miami Gardens, featuring a 3. 363-mile layout with 19 corners and qualifying speeds averaging 139 mph. Designed by Apex Circuit Design specifically for Formula One, it became part of the championship calendar in 2022 and hosts the annual Miami Grand Prix.

circuit:Monaco.title: Circuit de Monaco
circuit:Monaco.summary: The Circuit de Monaco is a 3. 337 km street circuit that winds through the urban streets of Monte Carlo and La Condamine, encircling the harbour of this small principality. Although officially designated as the Circuit de Monaco, it is widely known as Monte Carlo because the majority of the track passes through that specific district.

circuit:Netherlands.title: Circuit Zandvoort
circuit:Netherlands.summary: Located in the Dutch coastal dunes near Amsterdam, the Circuit Zandvoort is a 4. 259 km track that hosted the revived Dutch Grand Prix from 2021 until 2026. The circuit earns its nickname "The Roller Coaster in the Dunes" from its dramatic elevation swings and sharply banked corners like Tarzan and Hugenholtz, which wind through the North Sea's sandy terrain.

circuit:Qatar.title: Lusail International Circuit
circuit:Qatar.summary: Lusail International Circuit is situated north of Doha in Qatar and measures 5. 419 kilometers in length, featuring a primary straight spanning 1. 068 kilometers.

circuit:São Paulo.title: Autódromo José Carlos Pace
circuit:São Paulo.summary: Located in São Paulo, Interlagos is a 4. 309 km Brazilian racing circuit that opened in 1940 and was renamed in 1985 to commemorate Formula One driver José Carlos Pace, who perished in an aircraft accident eight years earlier. The counterclockwise track also features an adjacent kart facility bearing the name of fellow Brazilian racing legend Ayrton Senna.

circuit:Saudi Arabia.title: Jeddah Corniche Circuit
circuit:Saudi Arabia.summary: The Jeddah Corniche Circuit is a street racing venue situated along Saudi Arabia's Red Sea waterfront, serving as the home of the Saudi Arabian Grand Prix in Formula One since its inaugural running in 2021. The track has also begun hosting international electric racing competitions from 2025 onwards.

circuit:Singapore.title: Marina Bay Street Circuit
circuit:Singapore.summary: The Marina Bay Street Circuit is a street-based racing venue situated around Singapore's Marina Bay, spanning through the Downtown Core and Kallang districts.

circuit:Spain.title: Circuit de Barcelona-Catalunya
circuit:Spain.summary: Located near Barcelona in Catalonia, this 4. 657 km circuit is renowned for its balanced design featuring extended straights interspersed with diverse corner configurations, making it a versatile test for Formula One machinery. The track holds FIA Grade 1 certification and can accommodate over 140,000 spectators across its grandstands.

circuit:United States.title: Circuit of the Americas
circuit:United States.summary: The Circuit of the Americas in Austin, Texas is a 3. 426-mile FIA Grade 1 facility that serves as the permanent home of the Formula One United States Grand Prix. Beyond F1, the track hosts major international motorsport events including MotoGP, NASCAR, and world endurance racing competitions, having previously accommodated various other series ranging from IndyCar to rallycross.

driver:ALB.title: Alexander Albon
driver:ALB.summary: Alexander Albon is a Thai-British driver currently racing for Williams in Formula One, competing under Thailand's flag.

driver:ALO.title: Fernando Alonso
driver:ALO.summary: Spanish driver Fernando Alonso competes for Aston Martin in Formula One, having secured two world championships with Renault in 2005 and 2006 along with 32 Grand Prix victories over 23 seasons. Beyond his Formula One success, Alonso has achieved remarkable accomplishments in endurance racing, including two Le Mans 24 Hours victories and the 2018-19 World Endurance Championship, making him the sole driver to win both a Formula One drivers' title and a World Endurance Championship.

driver:ANT.title: Andrea Kimi Antonelli
driver:ANT.summary: Italian driver Andrea Kimi Antonelli secured the Formula One drivers' title with Mercedes in 2026, setting a record as the sport's youngest champion after claiming nine race victories since entering the sport in 2025.

driver:BEA.title: Oliver Bearman
driver:BEA.summary: Oliver Bearman is a British Formula One driver currently racing for the Haas team.

driver:BOR.title: Gabriel Bortoleto
driver:BOR.summary: Brazilian driver Gabi Bortoleto currently races for Audi in Formula One, competing under his shortened professional name after establishing himself as a promising talent in motorsport.

driver:BOT.title: Valtteri Bottas
driver:BOT.summary: Finnish driver Valtteri Bottas currently races for Cadillac in Formula One, bringing over a decade of experience to the grid. He achieved runner-up finishes in the World Drivers' Championship during consecutive seasons with Mercedes, and has secured 10 race victories throughout his 13-year career.

driver:COL.title: Franco Colapinto
driver:COL.summary: Franco Alejandro Colapinto represents Argentina in Formula One, currently driving for Alpine. The Argentine competitor has established himself as a driver on the grid's roster.

driver:DOO.title: Jack Doohan (racing driver)
driver:DOO.summary: Jack Doohan is an Australian driver currently competing in prototype racing for AF Corse in the Asian Le Mans Series, while maintaining a reserve driver position with the Haas Formula One team. He gained Formula One experience through seven race appearances across the 2024 and 2025 seasons.

driver:GAS.title: Pierre Gasly
driver:GAS.summary: Pierre Gasly is a French Formula One driver currently racing for Alpine. The 2020 Italian Grand Prix victory, achieved while competing for AlphaTauri, remains a significant milestone in his racing career.

driver:HAD.title: Isack Hadjar
driver:HAD.summary: Isack Alexandre Hadjar, a driver of French and Algerian heritage, races for Red Bull Racing in Formula One under French nationality.

driver:HAM.title: Lewis Hamilton
driver:HAM.summary: Lewis Hamilton is a British motorsport competitor currently racing for Ferrari in Formula One. The driver shares the record for championship titles with seven victories, while also holding numerous performance benchmarks including the most race wins and pole positions in the sport's history.

driver:HUL.title: Nico Hülkenberg
driver:HUL.summary: Nicolas Hülkenberg represents Germany on the Formula One grid, currently driving for Audi. Beyond his single-seater commitments, he has achieved significant success in endurance motorsport, most notably claiming victory at the prestigious 24 Hours of Le Mans in 2015 while competing for Porsche.

driver:LAW.title: Liam Lawson
driver:LAW.summary: Liam Lawson, a New Zealand-born racing driver, currently races for Racing Bulls in Formula One.

driver:LEC.title: Charles Leclerc
driver:LEC.summary: The Monégasque driver currently races for Ferrari in Formula One, having demonstrated strong performances throughout his career with nine Grand Prix victories to his name. Leclerc achieved his best championship result in 2022 when he finished as runner-up in the drivers' standings while representing the Scuderia.

driver:MAG.title: Kevin Magnussen
driver:MAG.summary: Danish driver Kevin Magnussen has returned to top-tier motorsport competition, currently campaigning in the World Endurance Championship as a factory representative for BMW with WRT after departing Formula One. His previous tenure in the sport spanned two separate periods, racing in the championship from 2014 through 2020 before rejoining the grid from 2022 to 2024.

driver:NOR.title: Lando Norris
driver:NOR.summary: Lando Norris, a British driver currently racing for McLaren, claimed the 2025 Formula One World Drivers' Championship with the team. Across his eight seasons in the sport, he has accumulated 14 Grand Prix victories.

driver:OCO.title: Esteban Ocon
driver:OCO.summary: French driver Esteban Ocon competed most recently for Haas in Formula One, having previously achieved a Grand Prix victory with Alpine at the 2021 Hungarian Grand Prix.

driver:PER.title: Sergio Pérez
driver:PER.summary: Mexican driver Sergio Pérez, known as "Checo," currently races for Cadillac in Formula One after finishing second in the 2023 championship standings while driving for Red Bull. Throughout his 15-season career in the sport, he has claimed six Grand Prix victories.

driver:PIA.title: Oscar Piastri
driver:PIA.summary: Oscar Piastri is an Australian Formula One driver currently racing for McLaren, having secured nine Grand Prix victories throughout his four-season career in the sport.

driver:RIC.title: Daniel Ricciardo
driver:RIC.summary: Daniel Ricciardo, an Australian driver known by his "Honey Badger" moniker, competed in Formula One for 14 seasons between 2011 and 2024, securing eight Grand Prix victories during his tenure in the sport.

driver:RUS.title: George Russell (racing driver)
driver:RUS.summary: British driver George Russell currently races for Mercedes in Formula One, having secured eight victories throughout his eight seasons in the sport.

driver:SAI.title: Carlos Sainz Jr.
driver:SAI.summary: Spanish driver Carlos Sainz competes for Williams in Formula One, having accumulated four race victories throughout his 12-season career in the sport.

driver:SAR.title: Logan Sargeant
driver:SAR.summary: American driver Logan Sargeant raced in Formula One during 2023 and 2024 before transitioning to endurance racing, where he currently competes for Ford in the FIA World Endurance Championship after previous stints in the LMGT3 category.

driver:STR.title: Lance Stroll
driver:STR.summary: Lance Stroll is a Canadian Formula One driver currently racing for Aston Martin, competing at the highest level of motorsport.

driver:TSU.title: Yuki Tsunoda
driver:TSU.summary: Yuki Tsunoda, a Japanese racing driver, holds a reserve driver position with Red Bull Racing and Racing Bulls. After competing as a full-time Formula One driver from 2021 through 2025, he transitioned to a reserve role for the 2026 season.

driver:VER.title: Max Verstappen
driver:VER.summary: Dutch-Belgian driver Max Verstappen has dominated Formula One over the past four years, securing consecutive world championships from 2021 through 2024 while racing for Red Bull Racing. Across his 12-season career, he has accumulated 74 Grand Prix victories and continues to compete for the team.

driver:ZHO.title: Zhou Guanyu
driver:ZHO.summary: Zhou Guanyu, China's sole Formula One competitor to date, raced in the sport between 2022 and 2024 before transitioning to a reserve role with Cadillac. He currently holds a development position within the Formula One grid while maintaining his status as the only Chinese-born driver to have competed in the championship.

team:Alpine.title: Alpine F1 Team
team:Alpine.summary: The Enstone-based team has competed as Alpine Formula One since 2021, representing Renault's sports car division while serving as the manufacturer's official works entry. Following Renault's withdrawal from the sport at the conclusion of 2025, the team transitioned from its previous identity as Renault F1 Team, which had operated under French automotive ownership and the broader Renault–Nissan–Mitsubishi Alliance.

team:Aston Martin.title: Aston Martin in Formula One
team:Aston Martin.summary: Aston Martin has been a recurring participant in Formula One history through different organizational structures, with the current iteration operating as AMR GP Limited under the Aston Martin Aramco Formula One Team banner.

team:Ferrari.title: Scuderia Ferrari
team:Ferrari.summary: Scuderia Ferrari represents the racing operations of the Italian luxury automaker and stands as Formula One's most enduring and accomplished competitor, participating continuously in the championship since its inaugural 1950 season. Nicknamed after their distinctive emblem, the team has established itself as the sport's benchmark for longevity and achievement across seven decades of competition.

team:Haas F1 Team.title: Haas F1 Team
team:Haas F1 Team.summary: An American-licensed Formula One outfit founded by NASCAR entrepreneur Gene Haas and launched in 2016, the team has operated under various naming arrangements throughout its existence. Leadership underwent a significant transition in early 2024 when Ayao Komatsu assumed the principal role, succeeding the long-tenured Guenther Steiner who had guided the squad since its establishment.

team:Kick Sauber.title: Sauber Motorsport
team:Kick Sauber.summary: Founded by Peter Sauber in 1970, this Swiss engineering firm initially built sports cars before joining Formula One in 1993 as an independent constructor. The operation underwent several transformations across its three decades in the sport before ceasing competition in 2025, having started more races than all but three other teams in history. Audi acquired the organization and its assets in 2024 to establish its own Formula One programme.

team:McLaren.title: McLaren
team:McLaren.summary: McLaren Racing operates as a British Formula One outfit headquartered at its Woking facility, functioning as part of the broader McLaren Group structure under Mumtalakat Holding Company's ownership.

team:Mercedes.title: Mercedes-AMG Petronas F1 Team
team:Mercedes.summary: Mercedes has participated in Formula One since 1954 as both a constructor and engine supplier. The current team, Mercedes-AMG Petronas, operates from Brackley under a German licence and has been jointly owned by Mercedes-Benz Group, Ineos, and Toto Wolff since 2022. The team carries the historic "Silver Arrows" nickname associated with Mercedes racing programmes.

team:Racing Bulls.title: Racing Bulls
team:Racing Bulls.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One team that joined the grid in 2024 as a constructor. Based in Faenza with operations in Milton Keynes, it operates as Red Bull GmbH's second Formula One entry alongside Red Bull Racing, providing a secondary team within the Austrian company's motorsport portfolio.

team:RB.title: Racing Bulls
team:RB.summary: Visa Cash App Racing Bulls is an Italian Formula One constructor that commenced competition in 2024, operating as one of two teams under Red Bull GmbH's ownership alongside Red Bull Racing. Based in Faenza with additional facilities in Milton Keynes, the team functions as a sister operation within the Red Bull motorsport portfolio.

team:Red Bull Racing.title: Red Bull Racing
team:Red Bull Racing.summary: Oracle Red Bull Racing is an Austrian-licensed Formula One team headquartered in England and owned by Red Bull GmbH. Founded in 2005 under the long-serving leadership of Christian Horner, the team transitioned to Laurent Mekies as team principal in 2025. Red Bull GmbH also operates Racing Bulls as its second Formula One entry.

team:Williams.title: Williams Racing
team:Williams.summary: Williams Grand Prix Engineering, currently competing as Atlassian Williams F1 Team in 2026, is a British Formula One constructor founded in 1977 by Frank Williams and Patrick Head following the collapse of Williams's previous racing venture. Headquartered on a substantial facility in Grove, Oxfordshire, the team has established itself as a significant constructor within the sport.
